title: Read an HTTP request
summary: Parse a raw HTTP request into method, path, query, headers and body.
hints: Split head from body first: head, _, body = raw.partition(' ').
The first line of the head is the request line. method, target, version = line.split(' ').
urllib.parse.urlsplit(target) gives you .path and .query; dict(parse_qsl(query)) turns the query into a dict.
For headers use name, _, value = line.partition(':') so a value like localhost:8000 keeps its colon.

quiz.question: Which part of an HTTP request tells the server what the client wants to do?
quiz.explanation: The method expresses intent: GET reads, POST creates, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE removes.

quiz.question: What separates the headers from the body?
quiz.explanation: Headers end at the first blank line; everything after it is the body.

quiz.question: Why are GET, HEAD and OPTIONS called safe methods?
options: They must not change data on the server
They don't need a Host header
quiz.explanation: Safe methods only read. That is why browsers and caches can repeat them freely, and why permissions often allow them for everyone.
